questions.q: A tank contains two immiscible liquids of densities $6\rho$ and $2\rho$. The higher density liquid is filled up to a height $L/2$ from the bottom. A thin rod of density $\rho$ and length $L$ is fully immersed and hinged at the bottom so that it can oscillate freely, as shown in the figure. If the rod is slightly disturbed from its equilibrium, the time period of small oscillations is $\dfrac{2\pi}{n}\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$, where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of $n$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $A$ be the cross-sectional area of the rod.

Mass of the rod, $M = \rho A L$.

Weight of the rod, $W = \rho A L g$, acting at a distance $L/2$ from the hinge.

When the rod is displaced by a small angle $\theta$, the restoring torque is provided by the buoyant forces from the two liquids.

Buoyant force due to the lower liquid, $F_{B1} = (6\rho) A (L/2) g = 3\rho A L g$.

This force acts at the center of the immersed part in the lower liquid, which is at a distance $L/4$ from the hinge.

Torque due to $F_{B1}$ is $\tau_{B1} = F_{B1} (L/4) \theta = (3\rho A L g) (L/4) \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Buoyant force due to the upper liquid, $F_{B2} = (2\rho) A (L/2) g = \rho A L g$.

This force acts at the center of the immersed part in the upper liquid, which is at a distance $L/2 + L/4 = 3L/4$ from the hinge.

Torque due to $F_{B2}$ is $\tau_{B2} = F_{B2} (3L/4) \theta = (\rho A L g) (3L/4) \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Destabilizing torque due to gravity is $\tau_g = W (L/2) \theta = (\rho A L g) (L/2) \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Net restoring torque, $\tau_{net} = \tau_{B1} + \tau_{B2} - \tau_g = \left(\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \rho A L^2 g \theta = \rho A L^2 g \theta$.

Moment of inertia of the rod about the hinge, $I = \dfrac{M L^2}{3} = \dfrac{\rho A L^3}{3}$.

The equation of motion is $I \alpha = -\tau_{net}$

$\dfrac{\rho A L^3}{3} \alpha = -\rho A L^2 g \theta$

$\alpha = -\dfrac{3g}{L} \theta$

This represents simple harmonic motion with $\omega^2 = \dfrac{3g}{L}$.

Time period, $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{3}} \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$

questions.q: The center of a disk of radius $r$ and mass $m$ is attached to a spring of spring constant $k$, inside a ring of radius $R>r$ as shown in the figure. The other end of the spring is attached on the periphery of the ring. Both the ring and the disk are in the same vertical plane. The disk can only roll along the inside periphery of the ring, without slipping. The spring can only be stretched or compressed along the periphery of the ring, following the Hooke's law. In equilibrium, the disk is at the bottom of the ring. Assuming small displacement of the disc, the time period of oscillation of center of mass of the disk is written as $T=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}$. The correct expression for $\omega$ is ( $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity):
questions.solution:
$E=\frac{1}{2} k(R-r)^2 \theta^2+m g(R-r)(1-\cos \theta)+\frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} \frac{m r^2}{2} \omega^2$ Differentiating wrt t , $\begin{aligned} 0 & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})^2 \cdot 2 \theta \frac{\mathrm{~d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left(2 \frac{\theta^2}{4}\right)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \cdot 2 \mathrm{v} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4} \cdot 2 \omega \frac{\mathrm{~d} \omega}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ \Rightarrow & 0=\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})^2 \theta \frac{\mathrm{~d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \theta \frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{mv} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2} \omega \frac{\mathrm{~d} \omega}{\mathrm{dt}}\end{aligned}$ Also, $\frac{d \theta}{d t}=\frac{V}{(R-r)} \Rightarrow \frac{d^2 \theta}{d t^2}=\frac{1}{(R-r)} \frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{1}{R-r} a \begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})^2 \cdot \theta \frac{\mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}+\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \theta \frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}=-\mathrm{mv} \alpha \mathrm{r}-\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2} \frac{\mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{r}} \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})+\mathrm{mg} \theta=-\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr} \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow-[\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})+\mathrm{mg}] \theta=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{~m}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^2} \\ & \Rightarrow-\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right]=\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^2}\end{aligned}$ Compering with standard equation of SHM $\omega=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right]}$ Hence answer is option(A) $\mathrm{OR}$
$\mathrm{kx}+\mathrm{mg} \sin \theta-\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{ma} \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{kx}+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\mathrm{x}}{(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})}-\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{ma} \\ & \mathrm{fr}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2} \cdot \alpha \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=\frac{\mathrm{ma}}{2} \\ & \therefore\left(\alpha+\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right) \mathrm{x}=\frac{3 \mathrm{ma}}{2} \\ & \therefore \omega=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right]}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: As shown in the figures, a uniform rod $O O^{\prime}$ of length $l$ is hinged at the point $O$ and held in place vertically between two walls using two massless springs of same spring constant. The springs are connected at the midpoint and at the top-end $\left(O^{\prime}\right)$ of the rod, as shown in Fig. 1 and the rod is made to oscillate by a small angular displacement. The frequency of oscillation of the rod is $f_1$. On the other hand, if both the springs are connected at the midpoint of the rod, as shown in Fig. 2 and the rod is made to oscillate by a small angular displacement, then the frequency of oscillation is $f_2$. Ignoring gravity and assuming motion only in the plane of the diagram, the value of $\frac{f_1}{f_2}$ is:
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{ML}^2}{3} \ddot{\theta}+\mathrm{K} \cdot \frac{\ell}{2} \theta \cdot \frac{\ell}{2}+\mathrm{K} \cdot \ell \cdot \theta \cdot \ell=0 \\ & \ddot{\theta}+\frac{15}{4} \frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{M}} \theta=0 \\ & \ddot{\theta}=-\left(\frac{15}{4} \frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{M}}\right) \theta \\ & \omega_1=\sqrt{\frac{15 \mathrm{~K}}{4 \mathrm{M}}}\end{aligned}$
$\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{ML}^2 \ddot{\theta}+2 \mathrm{~K} \frac{\mathrm{~L}}{2} \theta \cdot \frac{\mathrm{~L}}{2}=0 \begin{aligned} & \ddot{\theta}+\frac{3}{2} \frac{K}{M} \theta=0 \\ & \ddot{\theta}=-\frac{3}{2} \frac{K}{M} \theta \\ & \omega_2=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2} \frac{K}{M}} \\ & \frac{\omega_1}{\omega_2}=\sqrt{\frac{15}{4} \times \frac{2}{3}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{F}=-20\left(\mathrm{x}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=-20 \mathrm{X} \quad\left(\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{x}-\frac{1}{2}\right)$
$\therefore$ Particle will perform SHM about $\mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{2}$ with $\omega=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=\pi \mathrm{sec}$.
$\therefore$ Phase covered in $t=\frac{\pi}{4}$ second $=90^{\circ}$.
Given particle is at rest at $\mathrm{x}=1 \mathrm{~m} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=1$ is extreme position.
$\therefore$ In $\frac{\pi}{4}$ sec, it will be at equilibrium
$\therefore \mathrm{x}=0.5 \mathrm{~m}$ and momentum $=\mathrm{m} \omega \mathrm{A}=5 \times 2 \times 0.5=5 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Direction will be towards -ve $\mathrm{x}$.
Hence option (3)

questions.q: Two point-like objects of masses $20gm$ and $30gm$ are fixed at the two ends of a rigid massless rod of length $10cm$. This system is suspended vertically from a rigid ceiling using a thin wire attached to its center of mass, as shown in the figure. The resulting torsional pendulum undergoes small oscillations. The torsional constant of the wire is $1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 8}Nm{rad}^{- 1}$. The angular frequency of the oscillations in $n \times {10}^{- 3}rad{s}^{- 1}$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Given:

${m}_{1} = 30gm$ and ${m}_{2} = 20gm$.

Moment of inertia about the axis of rotation is

$I = {m}_{1}{{r}_{1}}^{2} + {m}_{2}{{r}_{2}}^{2}$

X-coordinate of the centre of mass can be written as,

${x}_{CM} = \dfrac{{m}_{1}{x}_{1} + {m}_{2}{x}_{2}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}} = \dfrac{0 + \left(20 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) \times \left(10 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}{\left(30 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) + \left(20 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)} = 4 \times {10}^{- 2}m = 4cm = {r}_{1}$

Therefore,

And ${r}_{2} = \left(10 - 4\right)cm = 6cm$

$∴ I = \left(30 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 16 \times {10}^{- 4}\right) + \left(20 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 36 \times {10}^{- 4}\right)$

$⇒ I = 1200 \times {10}^{- 7}kg{m}^{2}$

If the system is rotated by small angle ‘$\theta$’, the restoring torque is ${τ}_{\left(R\right)} = - k\theta$

And $\dfrac{{d}^{2}\theta}{d{t}^{2}} = \dfrac{- k}{I} \cdot \theta = - {\omega}^{2}\theta = \dfrac{- 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 8}}{1200 \times {10}^{- 7}} \cdot \theta$

$∴ {\omega}^{2} = {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ \omega = 10 \times {10}^{- 3}rad{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, $n = 10$.

questions.q: A particle of mass $1kg$ is subjected to a force which depends on the position as $\overset{\to}{F} = - k\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}\right)kgm{s}^{- 2}$ with $k = 1kg{s}^{- 2}$. At time $t = 0$, the particle's position $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)m$ and its velocity $\overset{\to}{v} = \left(- \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{2}{\pi}\overset{^}{k}\right)m{s}^{- 1}$. Let ${v}_{x} and {v}_{y}$ denote the $x$ and the $y$ components of the particle's velocity, respectively. Ignore gravity. When $z = 0 . 5m$, the value of $\left(x{v}_{y} - y{v}_{x}\right)$ is ______ ${m}^{2}{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
Given here: $\overset{\to}{F} = - k\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}\right)kgm{s}^{- 2}$ and $m = 1kg$

In x-direction, ${F}_{x} = - x = m{a}_{x}$

So, acceleration, ${a}_{x} = \dfrac{{d}^{2}x}{d{t}^{2}} = - x$

Now, for particle executing SHM, displacement along x-direction is

$⇒ x = {A}_{x}sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)$, here, angular frequency, $\omega = 1rad{s}^{- 1}$ and velocity, ${v}_{x} = {A}_{x}\omegacos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)$

Given at $t = 0, x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}m$ and ${v}_{x} = - \sqrt{2}m{s}^{- 1}$

So, putting the values, we get

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = {A}_{x}sin{ϕ}_{x}$ and $- \sqrt{2} = {A}_{x}cos{ϕ}_{x}$

From above two equations,

$⇒ tan{ϕ}_{x} = - \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

And ${A}_{x} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}m . . . \left(2\right)$

Similarly, along y-direction,

${F}_{y} = - y = m{a}_{y}$,

$⇒ {a}_{y} = \dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{t}^{2}} = - y$

So, displacement, $y = {A}_{y}sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right)$ and velocity ${v}_{y} = {A}_{y}\omegacos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right)$

Given at $t = 0, y = \sqrt{2}m$ and ${v}_{y} = \sqrt{2}m{s}^{- 1}$

So, putting the values, we get

$\sqrt{2} = {A}_{y}sin{ϕ}_{y}$ and $\sqrt{2} = {A}_{y}cos{ϕ}_{y}$

From above two relations, we have

$⇒ {ϕ}_{y} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} . . . \left(3\right)$ and ${A}_{y} = 2m . . . \left(4\right)$

Now, the value of $\left(x{v}_{y} - y{v}_{x}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right) \times 2cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) - 2sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) \times \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} \times 2\left(sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) - sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) \times cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)\right$

questions.solution:
Angular frequency for different values of spring constant will be given by, ${\omega}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{1}}{m}}$ and ${\omega}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{2}}{m}}$

$∴$ Time period $= \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{k}_{1}}} + \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{k}_{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{0 . 3} + \dfrac{\pi}{0 . 4}$

$= \pi \times \left(\dfrac{4 + 3}{12}\right) \times 10$

$= \dfrac{70}{12}\pi$

$= 5 . 83\pi$

Therefore, $n = 6$.

questions.solution:
Let the equation of $SHM$ be,

$x = Asin\left(\omegat\right)$

Here, $x$ is the position of the particle at any time $t$

$A$ is the amplitude of the $SHM$

$\omega$ is the Angular frequency of $SHM$

So, equation for the velocity will be,

$v = A\omegacos\left(\omegat\right) ⇒ v = {u}_{0}cos\left(\omegat\right) ( sincevelocityatt = 0is{u}_{0}, so\omega A = {u}_{0} )$

Now, during collision speed of particle was $( {u}_{1} ) = 0 . 5{u}_{0}$

and time be ${t}_{1}$

$0 . 5{u}_{0} = {u}_{0}cos\left(\omega{t}_{1}\right) ⇒ cos\left(\omega{t}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \omega{t}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} ⇒ {t}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{3\omega}$

As the energy will be conserve, so it will take same time to reach Equlibrium position first time,$i . e .$,
Time at which particle crosses equlibrium first time,

$( {T}_{1} ) = 2{t}_{1} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3\omega}$



Now, for the second half of the Oscillation, particle dosen't undergo collision that's why it will have normal Time period,$i . e .$

Time taken for the particle to go to the left will be $\dfrac{T}{4}$, as it was in the general case.

Here, $T$ is time period of $SHM$.

So to come back to Equlibrium position for second time time required will be $\dfrac{T}{2}$.

Now,

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} ⇒ \dfrac{T}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$

So total time required will be,

$\dfrac{\pi}{\omega} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3\omega} ⇒ \dfrac{5\pi}{3\omega}$

Here, $\omega$ is the angular frequency,$i . e .$, $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

Substituting it above we get,

$TimeTaken = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$
